docs.title: Fancy Demo Help
docs.text: Welcome to the help of the demo application. The demo shows the building blocks a desktop application gets out of the box: menus and actions, a Settings dialog, configurable keyboard shortcuts and notifications.

docs.title: Get help where you are
docs.text:
• Help Contents in the Help menu opens this page.
  • Context Help opens the help for whatever you are working in: put the keyboard focus there and use the Context Help shortcut. The Keymap page of the Settings dialog shows which shortcut that is on your system.
  • In the Settings dialog, the Help button opens the help for the selected page. It is disabled for pages without help.

docs.title: Topics
docs.text:
• Workspace: the main window of the demo.
  • Demo settings: the example pages of the Settings dialog.
  • Appearance, Keymap and Notifications: the built-in pages of the Settings dialog.

Use the navigation to open a topic.

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text: The Appearance page of the Settings dialog controls how the application looks: its color theme and the font used throughout the user interface.

docs.title: Open the page
docs.text:
1. Choose the Settings action. It is usually in the File menu.
  2. In the Settings dialog, select Appearance & Behavior and then Appearance.

You can also type a word such as "theme" or "font" into the search field at the top of the Settings dialog to find the page.

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
The Theme list sets the colors of windows, dialogs and icons.

Theme Effect System Follows the color scheme of your operating system. Light Light backgrounds with dark text. Dark Dark backgrounds with light text.

The application may offer additional themes. They appear in the same list.

docs.title: Font
docs.text:
• Font selects the font family for the user interface. Only scalable fonts are listed.
  • Size sets the font size in points, from 6 pt to 32 pt.

docs.title: Apply your changes
docs.text:
Changes take effect when you click Apply or OK. Cancel closes the dialog and discards changes that you have not applied. While the page has unapplied changes, a Reset link restores the values that are currently in effect.

The application remembers your theme and font and uses them the next time it starts.

docs.title: Demo settings
docs.text: The Demo Page 1 group of the Settings dialog holds example pages. They show the kinds of input elements a settings page can use: check boxes, radio buttons, lists, text fields, sliders, date and time fields and more.

docs.title: Open the pages
docs.text:
1. Choose the Settings action. It is usually in the File menu.
  2. In the Settings dialog, expand Demo Page 1 and Demo Subpage 1.
  3. Select Demo Subpage 1.1 or Demo Subpage 1.2.

docs.title: Change and keep values
docs.text: Change any value on a page. Apply stores the changes and keeps the dialog open; OK stores them and closes it; Cancel discards them. The values are kept for the next start of the application.

docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
The workspace is the central area of the main window. It has two parts, side by side:

  • on the left, a short description of the demo application;
  • on the right, the Notification Log, which lists the notifications the application has shown.

docs.title: Show or hide the Notification Log
docs.text: Choose Notification Log in the View menu. The application remembers your choice, and the width of both parts, for the next start.

docs.title: Try out notifications
docs.text: Choose Notifications in the Demo menu. The dialog that opens sends example notifications, which then also appear in the Notification Log. How each kind of notification is shown is set on the Notifications page of the Settings dialog.

docs.title: Keymap
docs.text:
The Keymap page of the Settings dialog lists the actions of the application together with their keyboard shortcuts. Use it to look up the current shortcut of an action, to assign your own shortcuts, or to go back to the default ones.

Help pages name actions as they appear in the menus and on this page. The shortcut of an action is not fixed: it depends on your platform, on the application's defaults and on your own changes. The Keymap always shows the shortcuts that are currently in effect.

docs.title: Open the page
docs.text:
1. Choose the Settings action. It is usually in the File menu.
  2. In the Settings dialog, select Keymap.

docs.title: Read the Keymap
docs.text:
The Keymap is a tree with two columns:

  • Action shows the action's name. Actions are grouped the way the menus are, starting with Main Menu. Expand a group to see its actions.
  • Shortcuts shows every shortcut assigned to the action. An action can have several shortcuts, or none.

Some actions have no menu entry, for example Context Help. They still appear in the Keymap, and you can assign shortcuts to them like to any other action.

docs.title: Change a shortcut
docs.text:
Right-click an action, or double-click it, to open its menu:

  • Add keyboard shortcut opens the Add Keyboard Shortcut dialog. Press the key combination you want to use and click OK. The new shortcut is added to the shortcuts the action already has.
  • Remove followed by a shortcut removes that shortcut from the action. There is one entry per assigned shortcut.
  • Reset to default restores the shortcuts the application originally assigned to the action. It appears only when the action's shortcuts differ from the defaults.

A key combination should trigger only one action. Before you add a shortcut, check that no other action in the Keymap already uses it.

docs.title: Apply your changes
docs.text:
Changes take effect when you click Apply or OK. Cancel closes the dialog and discards changes that you have not applied. While the page has unapplied changes, a Reset link discards all of them at once.

The application remembers your shortcuts and uses them the next time it starts.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: The application uses notifications to tell you about events, such as a task that has finished or a problem that needs your attention. The Notifications page of the Settings dialog controls how notifications are shown.

docs.title: Open the page
docs.text:
1. Choose the Settings action. It is usually in the File menu.
  2. In the Settings dialog, select Appearance & Behavior and then Notifications.

docs.title: Balloons and the notification log
docs.text:
A notification can appear as a balloon, a small popup in a corner of the screen:

  • A Balloon closes by itself after a short time. A progress bar shows the remaining time, and it pauses while the mouse pointer is over the balloon.
  • A Sticky balloon stays open until you close it.

Every notification is also recorded in the notification log, whether or not it appeared as a balloon. If the application shows the notification log, you can read missed notifications there.

docs.title: Do Not Disturb
docs.text: Select Do Not Disturb to stop all balloons. Notifications are still recorded in the notification log. Clear the check box to show balloons again.

docs.title: Balloon placement
docs.text: Balloon placement selects the corner of the screen where balloons appear: Bottom right, Bottom left, Top right or Top left. When several balloons are open, they stack from that corner towards the middle of the screen.

docs.title: Notification groups
docs.text:
Each notification belongs to a group, for example all notifications of one feature. The table lists every group of the application:

  • Group is the name of the group.
  • Popup type selects how the group's notifications appear: None (only in the notification log), Balloon or Sticky balloon.
  • Log shows that the group's notifications are recorded in the notification log.

To find a group quickly, type its name into the search field at the top of the Settings dialog. Matching groups are highlighted.

docs.title: Apply your changes
docs.text:
Changes take effect when you click Apply or OK. Cancel closes the dialog and discards changes that you have not applied. While the page has unapplied changes, a Reset link restores the values that are currently in effect.

New settings apply to notifications that arrive afterwards. Notifications that were already shown keep their original appearance.
